The second write passed the lint hook cleanly (no blocking-error notification, unlike the first attempt). The manifest is complete at `/out/ripgrep-3fce3b5-1/manifest.json`.

## Summary

Decomposed ripgrep (a ~57K-line Rust workspace of 10 crates) into **17 Logical Units**:

- **11 domain units**: `cli-flags`, `arg-resolution`, `search-orchestration`, `glob-matching`, `file-walking`, `matcher-trait`, `regex-engine`, `pcre2-engine`, `line-searcher`, `match-printer`, `index-engine`
- **6 infra units**: `cli-docs-and-completions`, `experimental-indexing-toggle`, `logger`, `diagnostic-messages`, `cli-utilities`, `grep-facade`

Most workspace crates (globset, ignore, matcher, regex, pcre2, searcher, printer, cli, index, grep) mapped one-to-one to a unit since they're already published as independently-seamed crates. The one large exception was `crates/core` (the `rg` binary itself, ~13.6K lines), which I split into 7 units along its real internal seams (flag parsing vs. arg resolution vs. doc/completion generation vs. top-level orchestration vs. the tiny indexing toggle vs. logging vs. diagnostic messaging), rather than treating it as one monolithic unit.

Work was done via 17 parallel `unit-scout` subagents (one per candidate), each independently verifying entrypoints, dependencies, and effects by reading the actual source. Two architectural findings surfaced and are recorded in `violations_observed`: unusually wide bidirectional coupling between `arg-resolution` and `search-orchestration`, and `cli-docs-and-completions` reaching into `cli-flags`' flag registry rather than a narrow API. All ~90 source files across `crates/*/src` and `crates/core` are partitioned; tests, examples, benches, docs, licenses, and build config are listed under `excluded` with reasons. `unpartitioned` is empty.

The lint hook (`ent ci --lint`) flagged one issue on the first write — an undeclared `subprocess` effect in `diagnostic-messages` (from its `std::process::exit` call) — which I fixed and the rewrite passed cleanly.
